segments.text: Hearsay is an out of court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
The Florida code lists exceptions in 90.803, where availability of the declarant is immaterial, and 90.804, where the declarant must be unavailable.

The spontaneous statement exception covers a description of an event made while perceiving it or immediately after. The excited utterance requires a startling event and a statement made under the stress of excitement.
For a child victim, the child victim hearsay exception requires a hearing outside the jury, a finding of reliability, and either testimony by the child or unavailability plus corroboration.

In a criminal case, always check the confrontation clause. If the statement is testimonial under Crawford, it is out unless the declarant is unavailable and there was a prior opportunity for cross-examination.
Business records need a custodian or a certification, and the record must be made at or near the time by someone with knowledge in the regular course of business.
